sources.title: A Comparison of Fractions Prepared from Navy (Haricot) Beans (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) in Diets for Germ-free and Conventional Chicks
sources.authorsOrOrganization: D. Hewitt; M. E. Coates; M. L. Kakade; I. E. Liener
sources.permittedUse: Direct conventional- and germ-free-chick comparison of raw and heated navy-bean meal, including body-weight and pancreatic outcomes.
sources.limitations: The controlled chick study does not provide a home feeding method, a complete ration, a universal inclusion rate, or evidence for another supported bird.

sources.title: The Utilization of Raw and Autoclaved Faba Beans (Vicia faba L., var. minor) and Faba Bean Fractions in Diets for Growing Broiler Chickens
sources.authorsOrOrganization: L. A. Rubio; A. Brenes; M. Castaño
sources.permittedUse: Direct growing-broiler comparison of raw and autoclaved faba-bean diets and fractions, including body-weight and organ outcomes.
sources.limitations: The studied varieties, processing, and diet levels are specific; this is not a household rule, complete ration, or other-species evidence.

sources.title: Raw Broad Beans (Vicia faba L.) as an Energy and Protein Source for Broiler Chicks
sources.permittedUse: Direct broiler-chick study of raw broad beans at defined dietary inclusion levels.
sources.limitations: The study’s defined formulated diets cannot set a household amount, a complete ration, or an outcome for a different species.

sources.title: Diet of Feral Pigeons (Columba livia) in Hawke's Bay, New Zealand
sources.permittedUse: Direct crop-content observation in free-ranging feral pigeons, including the named consumption of broad beans (Vicia faba) in a field-foraging context.
sources.limitations: The observational study does not identify processing, establish safety, prescribe a companion-pigeon amount or formula, or support another bean species or bird species.

sources.title: A Review on the Potential Food Application of Lima Beans (Phaseolus lunatus L.), an Underutilized Crop
sources.permittedUse: Maps source-specific antinutritional compounds reported for Phaseolus lunatus, including cyanide-producing glucosides, lectins, trypsin inhibitors, tannins, phytate, and oxalate.
sources.limitations: Does not study pigeons, define a pigeon dose, or establish a pigeon safety, processing, or formula outcome.

sources.title: Effects of Faba Beans with Different Concentrations of Vicine and Convicine on Egg Production, Egg Quality and Red Blood Cells in Laying Hens
sources.permittedUse: Documents vicine/convicine exposure and red-cell findings in laying hens; identifies the fava-specific compound concern.
sources.limitations: Does not study pigeons or establish any pigeon response, dose, safety rule, or raw-dried fava outcome.

sources.title: Comparison of Rhodanese Distribution in Different Tissues of Japanese Quail, Partridge, and Pigeon
sources.permittedUse: Documents tissue distribution of the cyanide-related enzyme rhodanese in adult pigeons.
sources.limitations: No cyanide or lima-bean exposure, dose, clinical endpoint, tolerance threshold, processing condition, or raw-dried bean outcome was tested.

sources.title: Activities of Thiosulphate and 3-Mercaptopyruvate-cyanide-sulphurtransferases in Poultry Birds and the Fruit Bat
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Femi Kayode Agboola, Bamidele Sanya Fagbohunka, and Gbenga Adebola Adenuga
sources.permittedUse: Documents rhodanese and 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase activity in pigeon tissues.
sources.limitations: No raw lima-bean feeding, cyanogenic-glycoside dose, cyanide tolerance threshold, clinical outcome, processing condition, or raw-dried bean outcome was tested.

sources.title: Influence of Dietary Phosphorus Concentrations on the Performance of Rearing Pigeons (Columba livia), and Bone Properties of Squabs
sources.permittedUse: Provides pigeon-specific dietary phosphorus context and describes plant-feed phosphorus as largely phytate-bound in the study background.
sources.limitations: Does not measure raw bean phytate or tannin, compare bean forms, or establish a pigeon safety or suitability outcome for any raw dried bean.

sources.title: Owner-approved precautionary pigeon policy for five raw dried bean forms
sources.permittedUse: Records the owner's explicit precautionary decision to classify raw dried lima, fava, black, pinto, and navy beans as avoid for pigeons because compound concerns exist and safe pigeon use has not been clearly established.
sources.limitations: This is a product safety-policy decision, not external proof of pigeon toxicity, a raw-bean feeding study, a preparation method, a nutrition value, a runtime formula rule, or a decision about another species or bean form.

sources.title: Nutritional Strategies for the Companion Parrot
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Susan Orosz, DVM, DABVP (Avian Practice), DECZM; LafeberVet
sources.permittedUse: Companion-parrot nutrition context that permits true berries such as blueberries in small amounts within an individually tailored feeding strategy.
sources.limitations: General companion-parrot veterinary guidance; it does not establish a quantity, a formula inclusion, a complete ration, an African-Grey-specific outcome, or an outcome for non-psittacine birds.

sources.title: Can Chickens Eat Blueberries?
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Chewy Editors; reviewed by Byron de la Navarre, DVM
sources.permittedUse: DVM-reviewed backyard-chicken context for plain fresh blueberries as a small occasional treat that does not replace complete feed, with washing and spoilage boundaries.
sources.limitations: Commercial owner guidance, not a controlled fresh-blueberry feeding trial, nutrient analysis, complete-ration formulation, universal serving rule, or evidence for other bird species or processed blueberry forms.

sources.title: Secret sauce: berries show potential to improve gut health and prevent gut-borne diseases in chickens
sources.permittedUse: Documents the agency's broiler research context for lowbush/wild blueberry pomace and related poultry microbiome outcomes.
sources.limitations: The reviewed form is blueberry pomace, not plain fresh raw blueberry; it cannot establish a fresh-fruit feeding outcome, a household amount, a complete ration, or a result for another species.
